full_judgment:
Syed Amirul Islam, J: This Rule was is-sued calling upon the respondent No. 1 to show cause as to why the unlawful enlistment of the petitioner's property at SI. No. 123 page 8765/1(3) of the Gazette Notification No. S.R.O. 365-1/86 dated 23.9.86 (Annexure 'K'-3) should not be declared to have been made without any lawful authority.

2. The petitioner is a private company limited by shares and incorporated under the Companies Act, 1913. The petitioner company has its factory and office at Tejgaon Industrial Area and for accommodating the labourers of the company it purchased a separate plot near Tejgaon measuring .15 acres of land in the name of the company in 1965 and constructed labour quarters (hereinafter called as said quarters). Immediately after liberation of Bangladesh the management and control of the company vested in the Government pursuant to the Presidents Order No. 16 of 1972 and thereafter the Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh vide Notification No. S.O.-II/IN-56/71/33, dated 7.1.72 declared all members of Agakhani Community as local and decided to give back the industries to them. Thereafter, vide Notification No. KDA—(M-1)3M-79/11 dated 28.10.77 the petitioner company along with its all assets were transferred by the Government to the former share holders of the petitioner company and as such the petitioner company was in possession of the case land after taking it back from the government but in early eighties same miscreants tried to trespass to the said quarters of the company and a criminal case was started by the company wherein the miscreants were found guilty and convicted but thereafter several miscreants, namely Md. Ali Hossain and others in order to grab the company's property filed Title Suit No. 384 of 1988 in the Court of First Assistant Judge, Dhaka, for permanent injunction and in that case the plaintiffs prayed for temporary injunction which was refused by the trial court and on appeal the said order was uphold by the appellate court. It is further alleged that besides the several miscreants others also continued to create similar problems in the said labour quarters and the petitioner company prayed to the government for help from time to time through letters written to the competent authority and in these circumstances beyond all expectations of the petitioner company they came to learn in, December, 1993 that the said labour quarters has been made abandoned property. Since the petitioner company did not know the exact forum where to submit their grievance they submitted three applications before the Divisional Commissioner, Dhaka, for delisting the said ease property from abandoned property list but subsequently the petitioner company came to know about the enlistment of the case property in the 'kha' list and as such ultimately filed a case before the Court of Settlement challenging the enlistment of the case property as abandoned property but that application was returned to the petitioner by endorsing on the body of it to the effect that the Court of Settlement cannot entertain the application as it has been filed after 2,665 days of the publication of the Gazette Notification and hence they moved this Court and obtained the instant rule.

3. During the course of hearing the petitioner company from time to time filed supplementary affidavits, wherein their main contention is that the property in question was always under the control, management and supervision of the company and the Government without serving any notice as required by Article 7(3) of P.O. 16 of 1972 most illegally and without jurisdiction enlisted the property in the "kha-list" which is par se illegal and without jurisdiction. Their further contention is that no notice under section 5(1)(b) of Ordinance No. LIV of 1986 have been issued and served upon the petitioner Company and as such the inclusion of the petitioner's property in "Kha list" is par as void and without jurisdiction.

4. The respondent No. 1 entered appearance and filed an affidavit-in-opposition wherein their main contention is that the case property comes within the ambit of Article 2 of P.O. 16 of 1972 and since the petitioner company was not in management, control and supervision of the said property on 28.2.72, the property became an abandoned property and the Government after proper enquiry enlisted the said property as abandoned property. It is further asserted that the petitioner company had full knowledge of the publication of the Gazette Notification dated 23.9.86 in respect of the abandoned properties along with the case property and that the case property has been correctly and lawfully enlisted in the "kha" 'kit of the abandoned property after proper enquiry and investigation. The case property is an abandoned property within the meaning of P.O. 16 of 1972 and one Faridul Islam, a cripled freedom fighter, and two members of shahid family, namely-Surjaban and Siddiqua Begum have been allotted the case property for their rehabilitation. It is further contended that the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 is a special statute which prescribed a limitation of 108 days for filing application before the Court of Settlement by an aggrieved party but in the instant case the petitioner company has not filed the case before the Court of Settlement within the prescribed porlod and filed the case after lapse of 2,665 days of the publication of the Gazette Notification and the Court of Settlement rightly rejected the application as being time barred. It is further contended that the petitioner company was in the knew of the publication of the Gazette Notification on 23.9.86 and as such filing of this writ petition after an inordinate delay renders this application as not maintainable on ground of inordinate delay. The respondent No. 1 also filed two supplementary affidavit-in-opposition wherein their main contention is that the property in question has been lawfully declared as abandoned property and the occupants themselves applied as back as in 1983 to the Government for allotting the property to them as the said property was an abandoned property and the whereabouts of the owners were not known and after due enquiry the Government being satisfied fixed rent for the property in question and asked the occupants to pay rent since 1.1.72. It is further asserted that an enquiry was held by a joint survey team and they found that the property answers the description of abandoned property and the whereabouts at the owner was not known. At that time the property was recorded in the name of one Amir Ali and his where about could not be traced out by the survey team and as such they opined that the property is an abandoned property and thus the enlistment of the case property as an abandoned property by the Government has been done after due compliance with all the legal requirements of the provisions of P.O. 16 of 1972 as well as Ordinance No. LIV of 1985.

5. The petitioner filed affidavit-in-opposition wherein their main contention is that at no point of time till enlisting of the property as an abandoned property, any notice whatsoever was served upon the petitioner company by the Government and thereby in enlisting the property as abandoned property the Government violated the mandatory provisions of section 5(1)(b) of the Ordinance. Their further contention is that after the release of the property by the Government in 1977 they are in continuous physical possession of the case property and before enlisting the same abandoned property the Government did not form any opinion as to whether the property in question is an abandoned property or not.

6. Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner Company made a lengthy arguments on merits of the Rule. His first submission is that the property of the petitioner Company cannot be declared as an abandoned property inasmuch as the petitioner Company is a Bangladeshi company and in support of his contention he relies on the decisions reported in 30DLR(SC)101, 1988BLD(AD)41 and 37DLR(AD)42. His second submission is that the petitioner company and its property and shares having been released by the Ministry of Industries, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh under Article 15 of P.O. 16 of 1972 holding the same not to be abandoned property, the Ministry of Works of the Government cannot treat the disputed property of the petitioner company as an abandoned property according to law and in support of his contention he relies on the decision reported in 37DLR(AD)42. The learned Advocate further submits that the presumption of conclusionness which is attached to the enlistment of property in the list of abandoned property is a rebuttable one and in the instant case the petitioner company has been able to prove by cogent evidence that the property in question is not an abandoned property and as such the property is liable to be de listed from the list of abandoned property and in support of his contention he relies on the decision reported in 49DLR(AD)161. The learned Advocate most emphatically submits that in the instant case the provisions of section 5(1)(b) of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1986 has not been complied with in including the case property in the `kha' list of the abandoned property and as such the publication of the Gazette Notification so far it relates to the case property is per se illegal and void. The learned Advocate further submits that since the property is not an abandoned property and the petitioner company had no means of knowledge about the inclusion of the case property in the `Kha' list they could not go before the Court of Settlement within the prescribed time of limitation and as such came before this Court. Hence the delay in the instant case should not stand in their way and the writ petition should be found to be maintainable, inasmuch as the petitioner Company has filed this writ petition for the violation of its fundamental right to property. In support of his contention he relies on the decisions reported in 51DLR(AD)241 and 4 MLR(AD)140.

7. Ms Naima Haider, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the respondent No. 1, on the other hand, submits that the enlistment of the property as such in the impugned list of the abandoned property is a conclusive proof that the property in question is abandoned property. The learned A.A.G. further submits that the onus is on the petitioner to prove that the property is not an abandoned property and no onus lies on the Government to prove that the property is an abandoned property. The Government is under no legal obligation to deny the assertion made by the petitioner in this writ petition and in support of her contention she relies on the decision reported in 49 DLR(AD)26. The learned A.A.G. further submits that the decisions relied on by the learned Advocate for the petitioner have no manner of application the facts and circumstances of the instant case and it is now well settled that even the property of a Bangladeshi citizen can be declared as abandoned property if it is found that on the fateful date, that is, on 28.2.72 the owner is found not to be in possession, control and supervision or management of the property and in the instant case it is abandoned clear from the papers annexed with the writ petition itself that the petitioner company was never in control, management and supervision of the property in question either on 28.2.72 or thereafter till the filing of the writ petition and in support of her contention she relies on the decision reported in 18BLD(AD)240. The learned Assistant Attorney General finally submits that even if it is conceded for argument's sake that no notice as required under section 5(1)(b) of the Ordinance has been served yet that will have no bearing upon the merits of the case in view of the fact that in the instant case there was no scope to serve any notice under the aforesaid provisions of the Ordinance inasmuch as the occupiers themselves admitted that the property in question was an abandoned property and applied to the Government for allotting the same to them treating the property as an abandoned property. The purpose of service of notice is to enable the owner/occupier to place their case before the Government before enlistment of the property and in the instant case the whereabouts of the petitioner company at the relevant time was not known and the company was not in management control or supervision of the property in question and the persons who were in physical possession of the property applied to the Government for allotment of the property to them, and in response to the said application the Government issued demand notice to the occupants and it is admitted by the petitioner company that ultimately the property has been allotted to one Faridul Islam, Surjaban and Siddiqua Begum and as such it does not lie in the mouth of the petitioner company to assert that the property in question is not the abandoned property or that it has been illegally enlisted as an abandoned property. The learned A.A.G. finally submits that once it is found that the case property answers the description of abandoned property it is immeterial whether it is enlisted in the 'Ka' list or 'kha' list and on the count the enlistment of the property as an abandoned property cannot be knocked down and in support of her contention she relies on the decision reported in 3BLC(AD)42.

8. We have perused the application, the affidavit-in-opposition, supplementary affidavits filed by the petitioner company, the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition filed by the respondent No. 1 and the affidavit-in-replies to the supplementary affidavits filed by the respondent No. 1 and the papers annexed therewith and considered the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the respective parties. In the instant case there is no dispute between the parties as to the status of the petitioner company and admittedly the petitioner company is a Bangladeshi company having its registered office in Bangladesh at the relevant time. So, the pertinent question that crops up in this matter for determination by this Court is as to whether the property of a Bangladeshi company i.e. in other words a property of a Bangladeshi citizen can be declared as an abandoned property if it is found that on 28.2.72 the owner was not either in occupation of the property or was not in management, control and supervision of the same. In the instant case from the averments made by the petitioner company in paragraph No. 5 which is wrongly typed as paragraph No. 4 of the petition it would be clear that they have admitted that the petitioner company along with its assets was declared as an abandoned property and taken over by the Government in 1973. Ultimately the Government took a policy decision that the Agakhanies residing in Bangladesh shall be treated not as non-locals and as such decided to give back the industries taken over as abandoned properties to the Agakhanies and pursuant to that policy on 31.10.77, 4760 shares were transferred to eight share-holders of the company who were available on that date along with the assets of the petitioner company. There was an Inventory made at the time of handing over the physical possession of the industry which has been annexed with the supplementary affidavit and marked as annexure 'V' wherefrom it appears that 4760 shares were transferred and not released to the former share holders of the company and the Industrial Units along with its pictures and structures were also handed over to the former share holders of the petitioner company but the disputed land in question was not given back to the petitioner company on 31.10.77. It thus appears that the petitioner company never called in question the taking over of the shares of the petitioner company along with its assets by the Government in 1973 as abandoned property and it is only on the change of policy of the Government in 1977 the shares were given back to the share holders of the petitioner company and it is not clear from the papers available on record as to whether it was given back to the former share-holders at their instance or by the Government on their own motion pursuant to the policy of 1973 that the Agakhanies will be treated as locals. It, thus, appears that in 1973 the Government rightly and lawfully declared the property as abandoned property and it is found that where they have transferred 4760 shares along with Industrial units they did not transfer the land in question to the petitioner company and the petitioner company did not also raise any objection to that nor took up the matter with the Government as to why the land in question has not been transferred along with other assets.

9. In the writ petition and in the affidavit-in-reply to the supplementary affidavit-in-opposition the petitioner company more than once asserted and reterated that since their purchase of the property in question in 1965 they were in continuous possession of the same until they were ousted from the property by the government on 15.6.94. But this assertion is proved to be false by the papers annexed to the writ petition itself. As for example on a perusal of Annexure "F' to the petition, that is, the judgment pronounced by the appellate court in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 50 of 1984 arising out of Title Suit No. 384 of 1983, it appears that in that case the positive case of the defendant respondent, that is, the share-holders of the petitioner company was that the petitioner company with its properties including the suit land (the case land, i.e., the present land) was temporarily taken over by the Government and that the defendant respondents are the owners of the Eastern Industries and the suit property and from the finding portion of the judgment it appears that the learned appellate court found that "admittedly the suit properties belonged to the defendant-respondents who are the proprietor of Eastern Industries and the suit properties were declared abandoned property by the Government when the defendant-respondents left the country during the war of liberation." The petitioner company accepted that finding and was fully satisfied with that observation of the appellate court and they did not feel aggrieved whatsoever by that finding of the appellate Court and that finding still stands and that paper has been annexed with this writ petition by no other person than the petitioner itself. It further appears that at least in 1983 the petitioner company was not in possession of the case property. One Md. Ali Hossain and others were found to be in physical possession of the case property by the appellate Court.

10. Annexure 'D' to the writ petition shows that the Government was pleased to transfer 4760 shares of the petitioner company to former share-holders along with the Industrial Units. Thus, it is clear from the Annexure 'D' that the shares along with the assets were taken over by the Government as abandoned property. We have already referred to the averments made in paragraph No. 5 of the writ petition and the statements made in paragraphs No. 4 of the affidavit-in-reply dated 6.6.99 and from that it appears that the petitioner company also admitted the fact that in 1980 Md. Eunus Khan, Mohammad Ali and few others were inducted as tenants into the case property by one Ruhul Amin Khan but no steps was taken by the petitioner company to evict /oust the said persons from the case land. On the other hand, it is found that as back as in 1977 the said Eunus Khan and others filed petition to the Government to allot the case land to them as abandoned property on the ground that the owner have left the country during the war of liberation and they (Eunus Khan and others) are in possession of the same. Not only this. It is the positive case of the petitioner company that they were dispossessed from the case land by "a group of miscreants in the company with unidentified officers of Ministry of Works and some police force forcively ousted the labourers from the said labour quarters on 15.6.94 and occupied it. That this statement of the writ petitioner is false is proved from Annexure 'F' to the writ petition. On a perusal of Annexure 'F' it appears that one Md. Ali Hossain and others instituted a suit for permanent injunction against Mr. Jumma Bhai and two others of which Mr. Jumma Bhai is the Managing Director of the petitioner company. In that suit the case of the plaintiffs was that the owner of the land is the petitioner company but during the war of liberation the shareholders left for Pakistan and the property was declared as abandoned property by the Government. When the property remained in uncared condition they (the occupiers) erected some "Dochala Tin sheds " therein and have been living therein with their families and they applied to the Government for allotment of the same. We have already stated that the case of the defendants, that is, the present petitioner company was that the industries of the defendant company with its properties including the suit land, that is, the present disputed land was temporarily taken over by the Government and that the defendants are the owners of the Eastern Industries Ltd. and the Government returned the property finally to the company along with other properties including the suit land vide Memo No. IND (M-1) 3M/79/11, dated 28.10.88. This memo has been annexed with the writ petition and marked as Annexure 'D' to the petition. But on a perusal of Annexure 'D' it does not appear that the case land was returned to the petitioner company rather it appears that 4760 shares of the company along with Industrial Units were transferred to the share-holders. The Inventory which was prepared at the time of handing over physical possession of the Industries has been marked as Annexure "V' to the supplementary affidavit dated 25.4.99. On a perusal of the Inventory it is found that the, case land was not given back to the petitioner company. Here we may profitably recollect the findings of the appellate court given in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 50 of 1984 which has already been quoted above. The appellate court also found that the plaintiffs Mohammad Ali Hossain and others were in possession of the property. It further appears that it is only in 1983 the petitioner company approached the Government not to allot the property to the occupants who have taken forceful possession in 1983 by ousting their workers. In this connection it may also be mentioned that the positive case of the petitioner company is that in the case land they had their workers coloney and their workers were living there as allottees but no paper has been annexed either with the writ petition or in the affidavit-in-reply or to the supplementary affidavits to show that any one of the workers of the petitioners company was ever allotted the quarters in the coloney or for that purpose they de-ducted rents from the wages of the allottees. Here it may also be mentioned that the property is situated within the city of Dhaka. It is contended by the petitioner company that they had constructed tin-sheds for accommodating the laborers of the company but site plan has been annexed to the writ petition or placed before this court to show that they had ever got any plan approved by D.I.T. for the construction of the labour quarters in the case land.

11. The Government has asserted in their affidavit-in-opposition that they have declared the case property as an abandoned property and they are in possession of the same through their allottees. This assertion of the Government has neither been controverted nor denied by the petitioner company. In this connection we may also refer to Annexure which is the copy of the application filed before the Court of Settlement and in paragraph (e) of that application it is asserted by the petitioner company that they have been owning and possessing the property as its labour quarters until now, that is, 2.5.94 and in paragraph (n) it is stated that the petitioner company is in possession of the land in question and the Government has not taken possession of the same at any time but from Annexure "K-2" it appears that on 16.4.94 the petitioner company wrote a letter to the Divisional Commissioner, the President of Abandoned Property Board requesting him not to allot the case property to any and here also they have admitted that this property has been enlisted in the 'Kha' list. In Annexure 'L' it is stated that after liberation of Bangladesh Government took the control and management of the company as abandoned property in 1973 and on approach of the Managing Director of the Company Government released the industry vide order dated 28.10.1977 from abandoned list. After released of the industry the petitioner company was in possession of all its assets including the case property but in December 1993 the petitioner company was surprised to know the case property was again enlisted as abandoned property. So, from their own assertion it is clear that in 1973 all the properties of the petitioner company along with the case property was taken over by the Government as abandoned property and that was never disputed by the petitioner company at any stage rather their case as it appears from Annexure 'L' is that after handing over the possession of the case land to the petitioner company on 31.10.77 the Government has again enlisted the property as an abandoned property but it appears from the materials on record that at no point of time till today the case property was never released by the Government to the petitioner company.

12. The first contention raised by Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam is that since the petitioner company is a Bangladeshi company its properties cannot be declared as abandoned property and in support of his contention he relied on certain decisions. To refute the contention the learned Assistant Attorney General relied on the recent decision reported in 18 BLD(AD)240. This case lays down the principle of law that in determining as to whether a property is an abandoned property or not the question of citizenship is irrelevant. Even the property of a Bangladeshi national can be declared as abandoned property if it comes within the definition of abandoned property as contained in Article 2(1) of P.O. 16 of 1972, that is, if the owner is neither in possession of the property nor in management, control or supervision of the same on 28.2.72. The petitioner company has miserably failed to establish that on that fateful date they were in control, management and supervision of the property rather their case as it appears from the writ petition as well as Annexure "L' to the writ petition is that the shares of the petitioner company along with its assets were rightly taken over by the Government as abandoned property in 1973. So, the case relied on by Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam on this point does not help him at all. The facts and circumstances of the case leads us to the irresistable conclusion that the share-holders of the petitioner company left this country during the war of liberation and that their whereabouts were not known on the fateful date of 28.2.72 and that they were not in control, management and supervision of the case land and thereby the land in question became abandoned property by operation of law and it appears to us that the Government has rightly declared the property as abandoned property.

13. Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate emphatically argued with all the force that he could command that the declaration of the case property as abandoned property is violative of provisions of section 5(I)(b) of the Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 and in support of his contention he relied on the decisions of the Appellate Division and submitted that these are mandatory provisions of law and if the Government wants of declared the property as an abandoned property notice has to be served either on the owner or on the occupant of the property and in the instant case the Government respondent has miserably failed to show that at any point of time they have ever served any notice upon either the owner or the occupier of the case land. In the instant case the admitted position is that the petitioner company was not in possession of the case property during the war of liberation and some other persons were in occupation of the same and as such no question of serving any notice upon the petitioner company does arise at all. In this connection it may further be mentioned that at the point of time the property was recorded in the name of one Amir Ali who is a share-holder of the company but Amir Ali does not come before this Court to assert that no notice was served on him by the Government before enlisting the property as an abandoned property and the question of serving any notice on said Amir Ali was also not possible because of the fact that his whereabouts were also not know and his shares were also declared abandoned and taken over by the Government in 1973. This fact is not disputed. It is therefore, clear that at the-relevant time said Amir Ali or the petitioner company was not in possession, control or supervision of the case property. The whereabouts, of the recorded owner was also not known. On the other hand, the admitted position is that the occupants of the case land as hack as in 1977 applied to the Government for allotting the property to them as abandoned property. Provisions as contemplated under section 5(1)(b) of the Ordinance relates to service of notice. Article 7(2) of P.O. 16 of 1972 provides that where any abandoned property is in possession of any person, such person shall within seven days of the commencement of P.O. 16 of 1972 surrender the said property to the prescribed authority. Similarly Article 7(3) provides that where the person in possession of any abandoned property fails to surrender such property as he is required to do under clause (2), the prescribed officer shall serve a notice on the occupant in the prescribed manner requiring him to surrender possession of the property. But in the instant case the occupants have never failed to surrender the possession of the case property rattier they voluntarily approached the Government to allot the property to them as an abandoned property. In their application they have specifically stated that the whereabouts of the owner was not known and as such they, have occupied it.

14. It, thus, appears from the facts and circumstances of the case that there was no necessity at all in the instant case to serve any notice upon the occupiers under Article 7(2) or (3) or P.O. 16 of 1972 inasmuch as at no point of time they have over disputed the status of the property as abandoned property rather right from the beginning they are in occupation of the property admitting the same to be an abandoned property. Thus we find substance in the submission of the learned Assistant Attorney General that in the instant case there was no occasion for the Government to serve any notice under Article 7 of the P.O. 16 of 1972 and non-service of any notice under Article 7 of P.O. 16 of 1972 is immaterial and not fatal at all.

15. The ,case property was enlisted as abandoned property in the 'kha' list on 23.9.86 and the instant rule was moved before this Court on 1.8.94 after about 8 years of the publication of the Gazette Notification. From the averments made by the petitioner company in piragraph No. 10 of the writ petition it appears that the petitioner company could learn only in December, 1993 that case property has been enlisted as abandoned property in the 'Kha' list. From Annexure H and 'I' to the writ petition it appears that the petitioner company were in the know that the case property is in occupation of the trespassers and the trespassers applied to the Government to get the allotment of the said property as abandoned property as back as on 6.7.83. Therefore, the statements made by the petitioner company that they came to know about the enlistment of the property as abandoned property in December, 1993 does not appear to be correct and it appears that right back in 1983 they knew that the occupants of the case property were trying to get allotment of the same from the Government as abandoned property and the same state of affairs is reflection the judgment of the appellate court in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 50 of 1984 which is annexed to the writ petition as Annexure 'E' which is dated 21.1.86. In Annexure 'F' there is a positive finding that the case property was declared abandoned property by the Government when the defendant respondents left the country during war of liberation. That was a contested order. Moreover from Annexure 'L' to the writ petition it appears that the petitioner company itself admitted that in 1973 the case property was taken over by the Government as abandoned property. We, therefore, are of the opinion that the petitioner company came to know that there property was taken over by the Government as an abandoned property in 1973 and as such there was no reason for them not to check the Gazette Notification which was published pursuant to Ordinance No. LIV of 1985. The reasons assigned by the petitioner company for this inordinate delay in tiling this writ petition do not appear to be genuine and sufficient. Of course, the question of delay was not considered by this court at the time of issuance of the rule but now on perusal of the records it appears to us that the petitioner company could not satisfactorily explain the delay and on that count also the rule is liable to be discharged. On the point of delay Mr. Kamal-ul-Alam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner company, relied on five decisions of this court of both the Divisions, namely 1990 BLD(AD)130, 1991BLD(AD) 227, 51DLR(AD)24 and 4 MLR(AD) 140. We have gone through the decisions relied on by Mr. Kamal-ul Alam but we are of the opinion that in the facts and circumstances of this case they have no manner of application whatsoever.

<u>16. A question may arise as to the legality of the enlistment of the property in the 'Kha' list because it is found that the Government is in possession of the property through their allottees. In that case it should have been published in the 'Ka' list. The learned Assistant Attorney General has submitted that once it is found that the property answers the description of abandoned property then it is absolutely immaterial in which list ii is published and the submission of the learned Assistant Attorney General is fortified by the decision reported in 3 BLC(AD) 42 wherein it has been held by the Appellate Division that once the property answers the description of abandoned property it is immetarial in which list it is published and on that count the publication of the property as an abandoned property cannot be set at naught.</u>

17. One of the points agitated by Mr. Kamal-ul Alam is that section 5(2) of Ordinance No. LIV of 1985 only lays down rule of evidence and the presumption of conclusiveness of abandoned property under section 5(2) of the Ordinance is a rebutable presumption. The learned Assistant Attorney General does not dispute this proposition of law but she submits that in the instant case the petitioner company has miserably failed to rebut the presumption. We find force and substance in this submission. On a perusal of the materials and papers on record it is obvious that the Government has legally declared the case property as abandoned property and taken over the possession of the same in 1973 and that action of the Government was never challenged by the petitioner company there is nothing on record to show that the case property was returned to the petitioner company in 1977 along with other assets. In paragraph No. 5 but wrongly typed as paragraph No. 4 at page 6 of the writ petition it is stated by the petitioner company "that immediately after liberation of Bangladesh the management and control of the company vested with the Government pursuant to President's Order No. 16 of 1972..... . In these facts and circumstances does it now lie in the mouth of the petitioner company to assert that the case property was not declared abandoned property by the Government or that the enlistment of the case property in the list of abandoned properties is illegal? Certainly not, more so when the statements of the affidavit-in-opposition has not been controverted.

In the result, the rule is discharged. However, there will be no order as to cost.

End.

Mvi. Md. Wahidullah, Advocate-on-Record ----- for the petitioner
Mr. Sharifuddin Chaklader, Advocate-on-Record ----- For Respondent No. 8

full_judgment:
Mainur Reza Chowdhury, C J:- This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 38 of 1987 discharging the Rule. 

2. The petitioner filed the above writ petition, the facts of which are that M/S. Afgania Hotel, hereinafter referred to as the Hotel in Khulna Town belonged to one Md. Buksh, nonlocal. After liberation of the country the owner being absent the Hotel and the building was declared abandoned property and the management of the Hotel as well as building was taken over under the provision of Presidents Order No. 16 of 1972. The Hotel was initially under the management of Ministry of Industries and that at one stage through a Notification dated 5th March 1973 published in the Bangladesh Gazette on 29th March, 1973 the management of the Hotel was placed at the disposal of the Bangladesh Parjaton Corporation. In pursuant to the advertisement for sale of the Hotel the petitioner submitted tender offering price Tk. 6,53,900/-. His offer being the highest the same was accepted and the matter of acceptance were communicated to him by the letter dated 22.5.86 signed by the Member Secretary, Subcommittee for disinvestment. In the light of the aforesaid letter of acceptance the petitioner deposited 25% i.e. an amount of Tk. 1,63,475/- of the total amount offered, towards down payment on 14.9.86. The petitioner by letters dated 16.9.86 and 30.9.86 requested the Secretary, Ministry of Industries as well as the member. Secretary Subcommittee for Disinvestment to hand over possession of the Hotel. The Ministry of industries by letter dated 23.10.86 requested the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna to hand over possession of the Hotel to the petitioner. As no step has been taken to hand over possession of the Hotel he was con-strained to file the above writ petition. 

3. It was the contention of the petitioner that he had performed his part by depositing 25% of the price offered as down payment, the respondents were under a legal obligation to hand over possession of the Hotel to him and that having not been done so the respondents, failed to perform their duties as required by law. The petitioner also filed Supplementary Affidavit before the High Court Division stated that the building in which the hotel was located became abandoned property was also held by the High Court Division in its judgment dated 3rd March 1980 passed in writ petition No. 1485 of 1974. In the Supplementary Affidavit it was asserted by the petitioner that the owner Md. Buksh acquired the property in 1948 and that the property in question was never within the periphery of Khulna Boro Bazar and the same was never made khas as per provision of section 20 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 and that fact of making the land and building in question khas was not published in the Gazette dated 14.3.1962 and that the owner Md. Buksh did not receive any compensation nor the Government took over possession and that the property in question was never under the control and management of the Government. The respondent Khulna City Corporation filed an Affidavit-in-opposition stating, inter alia, that the property in question situated within the property of Khulna Hat and Bazar and was acquired by the Government under section 3(1) and 3(2) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Upon initiating a proceeding being Misc. Case No. 1 of 1961-62 under section 20(2a) of the Act and that compensation Assessment Roll in respect of the property in question and other properties of the Khulna Bazar was made final and notification to that effect was made on 15th March, 1962 and that the said notification was published in Dhaka Gazette, Extraordinary dated 21th March 1962, that possession of the property was taken over by the Circle Officer (Revenue) Khulna Sadar and that the property was managed by the Government. Since the property in question was a property under the control of the Government the same did not assume the character of an abandoned property; that the person, by name Md. Buksh, who was running M/S. Afgania Hotel in portion of the building was absent after liberation of the country. The property in question being the property of the Government as could not be an abandoned property and that the property although mistakenly was treated as abandoned property for some-time managed through the Ministry of Industries and that at one stage notified for sale and the petitioner dropped tender to purchase the property but fact remained that the land and the building being the property owned by the Government was never an abandoned property and that at best as the Hotel that was owned by Mr. Buksh a non-local, could be abandoned business or Commercial concern, the petitioner was not entitled to claim the property in any respect and on any legal basis. The property being under the control of the Government could not be an abandoned property and Investment Board was not competent to sell the same as abandoned property. M/s. Afgania Hotel was located in a chandina property within the periphery of Khulna Boro Bazar appertaining C.S. Khatian Nos. 1254 an 1255 corresponding to S.A. Khatian No. 1 and the Plot Nos. (C.S.) 3288, 3289 and 3290 corresponding S.A. Plot Nos. 3288, 3289 and 3290 in Mouza Baniakhamar, Police Station Khulna, District Khulna. The Deputy Commissioner, Khulna on 17.4.84 handed over the property to the Khulna City Corporation and that the fact of handing over of possession to the City Corporation and that the fact of handing over of possession to the City Corporation was communicated to the Member Secretary, Sub-Committee for Disinvestment after taking over of possession. 

4. It appears that the question to be decided by the High Court Division i.e. whether the property in question was an abandoned property or it was a khas property acquired by the Government under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. The High Court Division after lengthy discussion and materials on record held that the property in question was made khas much long before the law as to abandoned property was enacted and en-forced. There is no provision in the Bangladesh Abandoned Property (Control, Management and Disposal Order, 1972 (President's Order No. 16 of 1972) that property in the possession or under the control of the Government under any law for the time being in force will assume the character of abandoned property. Section 20(2a) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and Ordinance No. 12 of 1960 was very much in force when President's Order No. 16 of 1972 was promulgated. In the back ground of the facts and the law, the property in question as was made khas under the provisions of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act upon initiation of Misc. Case No. 1 of 1961-62 and that Compensation Assessment Roll having been prepared in respect of the land of Mouza and published in the Dhaka Gazette, Extraordinary dated 21st March, 1962 in serial No. 7 at page 568 the same could not be an abandoned property in view of the provision of the President's Order No. 16 of 1972. The High Court Division therefore came to the conclusion that the property in question was not an abandoned property and whatever the respondent No. 1 Ministry of Industries did in the matter of the property in question was done upon averting from the material fact of making the property khas by the Government in the year 1961 and that at the material time the property was under the control of the Government and that Md. Baksh was a tenant of the Government.

5. The High Court Division also considered the question whether the petitioner was entitled to the relief sought. The undisputed position was that no document either an agreement or sale deed in respect of the property had been made in favour of the petitioner. Since there was no instrument was entered into creating a right in the property in favour of the petitioner, consequently the petitioner could not claim any right or interest that could be legally enforceable. It was submitted on behalf of the contesting respondents that the petitioner having no legal right could not invoke the extraordinary jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102(2) of the Constitution. The case of National Engineers Ltd. Vs. Director, Military Lands and Cantonment Directorate, Ministry of Defence, Dhaka Cantonment and others reported in 44 DLR (AD) 179 was referred to which held that as no specific legal right having been created in favour of the petitioner as regards the property in question the remedy sought was not available to him and as such the Rule so obtained was liable to be discharged on this ground too. The High Court Division, therefore, discharged the Rule. The High Court Division, from material before it found that the property in question was acquire and made khas prior to the promulgation of President's Order No. 16 of 1972. President's Order No. 16 of 1972 also provided that any property which is under the control or invested in the Government under any law in force, could not be an abandoned property under President's Order No. 16 of 1972. The petitioner in the instant case, therefore, could not claim relief of completing the sale and handing over possession of M/s. Afgania Hotel to him as an auction purchase of a property which was sold as an abandoned property but in fact, the same is not an abandoned property. The impugned judgment and order do not suffer from any illegality. The petition is, therefore, dismissed. 

End.

full_judgment:
Quazi Shafi Uddin , J: This Rule is directed against the judgment and decree dated 16.9.92 and 21.9.92 respectively passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Chuadanga, in Title Appeal No. 126 of 1989 affirming the judgment and decree dated 19.4.89 and 24.4.89 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Damurhuda, Chaudanga in Title suit No. 60 of 1984.

2. The plaintiff petitioner filed a title suit in the Court of Assistant Judge, Damurhuda Chuadanga for declaration of title and also for declaration that the suit property is not an abandoned property. Plaintiff became the owner by purchase and has been in possession in the suit property but the property was wrongly recorded in the name of opposite party No. 1 in S.A. Khatian and the same was also wrongly enlisted as an abandoned property which creates cloud over the right, title and interest of the plaintiff Hence the plaintiff filed a suit for declaration of title and also for a declaration that the property is not an abandoned properly.

3. The defendant No. 2 and 3 contested the suit denying all the material allegation made in the plaint. The suit property was recorded in the name of defendant No. 1 Hasina Jamil, defendant No. 1 was a non bengali and after her departure the suit property became an abandoned property.

4. After hearing both the parties the learned Assistant Judge, Damurhuda, Chuadanga by his judgment and decree dismissed the suit on the ground that the suit is barred by limitation and that the plaintiff could not prove his title and possession. The defendant No. 1 being a non bengali, left the country and the property was enlisted as an abandoned property.

5. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree an appeal was filed by the plaintiff and the appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Chuadanga who affirmed the judgment of the trial court but dismissed the appeal on some other grounds. Against the aforesaid judgment and decree a revisional application was filed before this court and obtained the present rule.

<u>6. The defendant Nos. 2 and 3 namely the Government filed written statement and contended that the S.A. Khatian was rightly prepared in the name of defendant No. 1. Defendant No. 1 a non-Bengali and after her departure the property was enlisted as an abandoned property. The learned Additional District Judge, observed that though the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 claimed that the property was enlisted as an abandoned property as the defendant No. 1 left the country but the Government could not show any paper regarding that title of the defendant No. 1. Although the S.A. Khatian stood in the name of Hasina Jamil but the S.A. Khatian cannot confer any title in respect of any landed property to anybody. The learned Judge found that the suit property as per schedule of the plaint is 1.29 acres of land which appertains to plot No. 38 of C.S. Khatian No. 179 but unfortunately, the said property was not found in C.S. Khatian No. 179. The learned Judge also found from Ext. 1 the sale deed normally registered on 30.3.39 and he purchased the property of C.S. plot No. 28 and not C.S. plot No. 38 of S.A. Khatian No. 179. Accordingly the learned Judge dismissed the suit and. affirmed the judgment and decree of the trial court, upon a reading of C.S. Khatian Ext. 3 (a) not Ext. 3 as the learned Judge referred the C.S. Khatian No. 179 and the hal khatian No. 422, dag as stated as 38 but quantity of land measured 1.29 acres of land was sold. The learned Judge termed the discrepancy as simple anomally. The judgment of the trial court shows that the learned Judge found that the plaintiff failed to prove his title and possession in the suit land and that the property is an abandoned property. Court of appeal below has found that the property is not an abandoned property. Government failed to prove that the property is an abandoned property. Mere recording in the S.A. Khatian could not confer any title and as such the learned Additional District Judge found that the property is not an abandoned property. Furthermore the said defendant No. 1 Hasina Jamil has not appeared and contest at the suit and did not file any written statement or adduced any evidence and as such her title could not be proved. The record of S.A. Khatian cannot also stand. Since the property is not recorded in the S.A. Khatian and the Government could not also prove the suit property as an abandoned property. The only issue that remains whether the plaintiff has been able to prove his title in the suit land. It is stated that Fakir Chand Zoarder, Tustu Zoarder and Hazu Bewa were the C.S. recorded tenants of the suit property and Ship Kumari Debi was their land lady. The said Fakir Chand Zoarder sold his share of 1.30 acres of land to Karam Ali Biswas by a registered kabala dated 30.3.39. Karam Ali Biswas died leaving behind a son Abu Hannan and 2 daughters namely Nurjahan and Forjan. Nurjahan sold .97 acres of land to the plaintiff petitioner by a registered kabala dated 12.8.68. Subsequently Forjan sold .33 acres of land to defendant No. 2 by a registered kabala dated 8.01.76. This kabala was exhibited and the plaintiff also deposed that the defendant vendors in this way transferred their shares to the plaintiffs and they are in possession of the suit property by the aforesaid purchase. P.W. 2 also stated that the plaintiff purchased the suit property and since then they are in possession by cultivating the land. P.W.3 also corroborated the evidence of P.W.1 and 2 about title and possession of the plaintiff. D.W.1 has also deposed in his cross -examination that the C.S. record was not submitted showing the name of Hasina Jamil and he has never seen Hasina Jamil. The suit property was not declared as abandoned property and he has not associated with their act declaring the property as abandoned property. The .appellate court observed that the property is not an abandoned property. Since the plaintiffs have been able to prove their title by purchase and also have been able to prove their possession, the court illegally dismissed the suit. The learned Additional District Judge misread the C.S. khatian No. 179 and found that there is no such C.S. plot No. 38 in the said C.S. Khatian. The judgment and decree passed by the courts below are not sustainable in law.</u>

7. In the result, the rule is made absolute and the judgment and decree passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Chuadanga in Title Appeal No. 126 of 1989 and the judgment and decree dated 19.4.1989 and 24.4.1989 respectively passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Damurhuda, Chuadanga in Title Suit No. 60 of 1984 are hereby set aside. The suit is decreed and the title of the plaintiff in the suit land is declared. The S.A. Khatian in which the name of Hasina Jamil was recorded is wrong. The property is not an abandoned property.

Send down the lower court records at once.

End.
